title: [RPG Design Guides] Naming Proper Nouns (People, Places, etc.)

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】固有名詞（人名・地名等）の命名
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] Naming Proper Nouns (People, Places, etc.)

blocks.source: 創作における固有名詞の命名に付いて考えてみる。ちなみに、RPGに限定した内容ではないので、小説や漫画にも流用可能なはず。
blocks.translation: Let's consider naming proper nouns in creative works. Incidentally, this isn't limited to RPGs, so it should also be applicable to novels and manga.

blocks.source: 名前の役割は第一に識別にある。よって、作品全体を通して覚えやすい名前を考えていきたい。命名に困ったという時もこれを見て参考にして頂ければ幸い。
blocks.translation: The primary role of a name is identification. Therefore, I want to consider names that are easy to remember throughout the entire work. If you're having trouble coming up with names, I hope you can use this as a reference.

blocks.source: ぶっちゃけ好みでいいっちゃいいんですけどね……。所詮はネーミングセンスの問題なので、だいぶ筆者の主観が入ってるような気もします。その辺は多めに見てくだされば。
blocks.translation: To be honest, you can simply go with whatever you like... Since it's ultimately a matter of naming sense, I feel that this is heavily influenced by the author's personal opinions. I hope you'll be lenient about that.

blocks.source: 似た様な名前を付けない
blocks.translation: Don't Give Characters Similar Names

blocks.source: 同一作品中で、似たような名前のキャラクターがいると、プレイヤーを混乱させやすい。中でも『ア行』『サ行』『ラ行』等は語感がよいので使われやすいが、同じ文字を多用し過ぎると、似たような名前が多くなってしまうので注意。
blocks.translation: If characters in the same work have similar names, players can easily become confused. Sounds such as "a," "sa," and "ra" are especially popular because they sound pleasant, but be careful: using the same sounds too often will result in many similar names.

blocks.source: 例えば、『アルス』と『アレク』は頭文字や文字数が同じなので区別しにくい。文字数が同じなのは仕方ないにしても、頭文字には気を付けたい。人間は名前を脳内で読み上げる場合、頭文字を最初に意識するもの。つまり『エリス』と『クリス』なら前の例よりも、まだ区別が容易となる。
blocks.translation: For example, "Ars" and "Alec" are difficult to distinguish because they have the same initial and the same number of letters. There's no helping the fact that they have the same number of letters, but you should pay attention to their initials. When people read names aloud in their heads, they are conscious of the initial first. In other words, "Eris" and "Chris" are still easier to distinguish than the previous example.

blocks.source: 頭文字や文字数が異なっていても、雰囲気の似た名前の人物が多く集まると混同しやすくなる。ありきたりな名前ばかりでもいけないし、風変わりな名前ばかりでも良くない。
blocks.translation: Even if the initials and number of letters are different, having many characters with names that evoke a similar impression can make them easy to confuse. You shouldn't use only commonplace names, but using only unusual names isn't good either.

blocks.source: ありきたりな名前が集まってしまった例
blocks.translation: An Example of Too Many Ordinary Names

blocks.source: ジョン、トム、ビリー、デビッド
blocks.translation: John, Tom, Billy, David

blocks.source: 山田、田中、佐藤、鈴木
blocks.translation: Yamada, Tanaka, Sato, Suzuki

blocks.source: 変わった名前、長い名前が集まってしまった例
blocks.translation: An Example of Too Many Unusual or Long Names

blocks.source: ジェファーソン、エイブラハム、ラザフォード、ベンジャミン
blocks.translation: Jefferson, Abraham, Rutherford, Benjamin

blocks.source: 五十嵐、九十九、我孫子、生田目
blocks.translation: Igarashi, Tsukumo, Abiko, Namatame

blocks.source: メリハリを意識しよう
blocks.translation: Be Mindful of Contrast

blocks.source: そこで『平凡な名前』と『変な名前』等、雰囲気の異なる名前を適度に織り交ぜると、メリハリが付いて覚えやすくなる。山田と五十嵐のように雰囲気が異なる名前の人物を混同することは少ないはず。
blocks.translation: Mixing names with different impressions, such as "ordinary names" and "strange names," in moderation will create contrast and make them easier to remember. People with names that feel different, such as Yamada and Igarashi, are unlikely to be confused with each other.

blocks.source: 『変な名前』と書いたけれど、創作の世界ではいわゆる『DQNネーム』『キラキラネーム』に該当する様な珍名も許容される。物語の登場人物は作者からすれば、子供の様な物であるが、現実の子供と違って名前でイジメられたりはしないからだ（※）。むしろ『識別』という目的には多少のキラキラも、メリハリが付いて有用と言える。
blocks.translation: I called them "strange names," but in the world of fiction, unusual names corresponding to so-called "DQN names" or "kirakira names" are acceptable. From the author's perspective, the characters in a story are like children, but unlike real children, they won't be bullied because of their names (※). In fact, when it comes to the purpose of "identification," a little sparkle can be useful because it creates contrast.

blocks.source: ※作中でイジメられるかもしれないが、それはそれでキャラ作りとしてはおいしいので置いておく。
blocks.translation: ※They might be bullied in the story, but I'll leave that aside, since it would be a delicious opportunity for character development.

blocks.source: イメージに合った名前を付ける
blocks.translation: Choose Names That Match the Image

blocks.source: 主人公に『カッコいい名前』、ヒロインに『綺麗な名前』、悪役に『悪そうな名前』、子供に『可愛い名前』、色物キャラに『変な名前』、平凡キャラや脇役に『平凡な名前』。という様にキャラクターや地名のイメージにあった名前を付けよう。
blocks.translation: Give the protagonist a "cool name," the heroine a "beautiful name," the villain an "evil-sounding name," children "cute names," comic-relief characters "strange names," and ordinary characters or supporting characters "ordinary names." In this way, choose names that match the image of the character or place.

blocks.source: ただし、どんな名前が『カッコいい』のかという、かなり個人の感性に依存するので、あまり詳しくは書けない。例えば、濁音が入ると『強そう』『悪そう』等とは、よく言われる。
blocks.translation: However, I can't go into much detail because what makes a name "cool" depends heavily on individual sensibilities. For example, people often say that names containing voiced sounds seem "strong" or "evil."

blocks.source: 文字数を意識してみる
blocks.translation: Consider the Number of Letters

blocks.source: ３、４文字の名称は適度な長さで発音もしやすく無難だけれど、それだけにありふれた物になりやすい。そこで、２文字や５文字以上の名前をアクセント的に入れてみよう。２文字の名前は可愛らしい印象がするためか、子供や動物キャラに多い印象。５文字以上で濁音が多いと凄く悪者っぽい。『バルバトス』とか、名前だけでもう現行犯逮捕しても良いと思う。
blocks.translation: Names with three or four letters are a moderate length, easy to pronounce, and safe choices, but for that very reason they tend to be commonplace. So try adding two-letter names or names with five or more letters as accents. Two-letter names tend to give a cute impression, which may be why they are often used for children and animal characters. A name with five or more letters and many voiced sounds feels extremely villainous. Take "Barbatos," for example—I feel like the name alone is enough to arrest him in the act.

blocks.source: 言うまでもなく５文字、６文字みたいな長い名前を多用するのは覚えづらくなるので注意。あくまでもアクセントとして使おう。
blocks.translation: Needless to say, using too many long names of five or six letters will make them difficult to remember, so be careful. Use them only as accents.

blocks.source: 末尾に注目してみる
blocks.translation: Pay Attention to the Endings

blocks.source: 他と雰囲気の違う人名にしたい、と思った場合は末尾の文字の母音に注目してみよう。実は多くの西洋風RPGでは、人名末尾に使われる母音の使用頻度に非常に大きなバラツキがある。
blocks.translation: If you want to give someone a name with a different feel from the others, pay attention to the vowel at the end. In fact, in many Western-style RPGs, there is a very significant variation in how frequently each vowel is used at the end of people's names.

blocks.source: 具体的には……
blocks.translation: Specifically...

blocks.source: ア、ウ ＞ イ、オ、ン ＞ エ
blocks.translation: A, U > I, O, N > E

blocks.source: という具合だ。正式に調査したわけではないが、これは単に現実の西洋人の名前が、そうなっているというだけの理由だと思われる。よって、DQでもFFでも、西洋風RPGなら大体同じ法則が成り立つ。特に母音が『アウ』の中でも『アナラスル』辺りが末尾に来る頻度は非常に高い。
blocks.translation: That's the general pattern. I haven't conducted a formal study, but this is probably simply because real Western names tend to follow that pattern. Therefore, whether it's DQ or FF, more or less the same rule applies to Western-style RPGs. In particular, among names ending in the A or U sounds, endings such as "a," "na," "ra," "sa," and "ru" occur very frequently.

blocks.source: というわけで、意識して『イオンエ』の母音で終わる名前を作れば、他と差別化できるはず。また『アウ』の母音でも『タダハバパヤワウツヅヌフブプムユ』辺りは頻度が下がるので、使ってみよう。
blocks.translation: Therefore, deliberately creating names that end with the vowels I, O, N, or E should help distinguish them from others. Even among names ending in A or U, sounds such as ta, da, ha, ba, pa, ya, wa, u, tsu, dzu, nu, fu, bu, pu, mu, and yu are less frequent, so try using them.

blocks.source: 中でも末尾に『エ』の母音が来る頻度は意外なほど低い。例えば、DQやFFのメインキャラクターで該当の人物を思い浮かべても、ほとんど出てこないはず。これを読んでいる人の中で、創作をしているという方は是非、メインの登場人物に、末尾に『エ』の母音で終わる名前を付けてみよう。
blocks.translation: In particular, names ending in the vowel E occur surprisingly rarely. For example, even if you try to think of a DQ or FF main character with such a name, hardly any should come to mind. If you're reading this and creating a work of your own, by all means give one of your main characters a name ending in the vowel E.

blocks.source: もっとも、別に『アナラスル』初め『アウ』音が末尾に来ることを徹底的に避ける必要はない。これらは現実に発音しやすく、耳に馴染みやすいから、多用されていると考えられるからだ。そればっかりにならないように注意すれば十分だろう。
blocks.translation: That said, there's no need to rigorously avoid names ending in sounds such as "a," "na," "ra," "sa," and "ru," or A and U sounds in general. They are probably used frequently because they are easy to pronounce in real life and pleasant to the ear. It should be enough simply to avoid using them exclusively.

blocks.source: 前後を飾ってみる
blocks.translation: Decorate the Names

blocks.source: 固有名詞の前後を特徴や敬称などで、飾ってみよう。固有名詞そのものの話ではないけれど、識別子としての役割を考えた場合に有効な手法となる。
blocks.translation: Try embellishing proper nouns with characteristics, honorifics, and the like before or after them. This isn't about the proper nouns themselves, but it is an effective technique when considering their role as identifiers.

blocks.source: 国なら：○○○王国、○○○帝国、○○○共和国
blocks.translation: For countries: the Kingdom of XXX, the XXX Empire, the Republic of XXX

blocks.source: 町なら：貿易都市○○○、首都○○○、辺境の村○○○
blocks.translation: For towns: the trading city of XXX, the capital of XXX, the frontier village of XXX
For people: King XXX, Emperor XXX, His Majesty XXX, His Holiness XXX, General XXX, Count XXX

blocks.source: この方法なら、固有名詞自体を覚えてもらえなくとも、一応の区別は付く。単に固有名詞を並べるよりは、世界観も深まるし、プレイヤーもイメージしやすいはず。
blocks.translation: With this method, people can still distinguish them even if they don't remember the proper nouns themselves. Compared with simply listing proper nouns, it also deepens the worldbuilding and should make it easier for players to form an image.

blocks.source: 言うまでもなく、敬称や爵位、階級などを使用する場合は、ちゃんと意味を調べておこう。上下関係を間違えたりすると、恥をかくことになる。
blocks.translation: Needless to say, if you use honorifics, titles of nobility, ranks, or the like, be sure to look up their meanings properly. Getting the hierarchy wrong could make you look foolish.

blocks.source: 参考までに実例
blocks.translation: Some Examples for Reference

blocks.source: 公爵＞侯爵＞伯爵＞子爵＞男爵
blocks.translation: Duke > Marquess > Count > Viscount > Baron

blocks.source: 元帥＞大将～少将＞大佐～少佐＞大尉～少尉＞曹長
blocks.translation: Marshal > General–Major General > Colonel–Major > Captain–Second Lieutenant > Sergeant Major

blocks.source: ちなみに『猊下』とは法皇・教皇など、偉い聖職者のことを指す敬称らしい。ただし『げいか』と正しく読める人間がどの程度いるかは怪しいので、別の言葉を使ったほうが良いかも。例えば、ＸＸＸＸ教皇とそのまま役職名で呼ばせても良いし、『陛下』などを代わりに使っても良い。『猊下』と同様の意味で『聖下』『台下』等という言葉もあるそうな。
blocks.translation: Incidentally, "His Holiness" is apparently an honorific referring to an important clergyman, such as a pontiff or pope. However, it's questionable how many people can correctly read the Japanese term "geika," so it may be better to use a different word. For example, you could have someone address them by their official title, such as Pope XXXX, or use something like "His Majesty" instead. Apparently, terms such as "His Sanctity" and "Your Eminence" can also have a similar meaning to "His Holiness."

blocks.source: まとめ
blocks.translation: Conclusion

blocks.source: 名前は識別子であるゆえに、キャラクター間のバランスを考慮しながら、分かりやすさ・覚えやすさを重視した命名をしよう。創作人物の名前に限り、メリハリのために変な名前を付けることも時には有効だ。
blocks.translation: Since names are identifiers, prioritize clarity and memorability while considering the balance among your characters. When naming fictional characters, giving them strange names can sometimes be effective for creating contrast.

blocks.source: でも、自分の子供には『DQNネーム』を付けないように気を付けよう。将来、名前が原因で子供がグレてしまったら目も当てられない。
blocks.translation: However, be careful not to give your own children "DQN names." If your child becomes a delinquent in the future because of their name, it would be an unbearable situation.

lines.source: とりあえず、[[LINK_1]]ラストバイブル3[[/LINK_1]]のヒロインに『モチョワ』と付けるネーミングセンスはちょっとどうかと思った。でも、インパクト勝負と考えればアリなのか……？

parts.source: のヒロインに『モチョワ』と付けるネーミングセンスはちょっとどうかと思った。でも、インパクト勝負と考えればアリなのか……？

lines.translation: For now, I have to say that naming the heroine of [[LINK_1]]Last Bible 3[[/LINK_1]] “Mochowa” seems like a bit much. But if the goal is to make an impact, maybe it works...?

For example, you could have someone address them by their official title, such as Pope XXXX, or use something like "His Majesty" instead. Apparently, terms such as "His Sanctity" and "Your Eminence" can also have a similar meaning to "His Holiness."
texts.名前は識別子であるゆえに、キャラクター間のバランスを考慮しながら、分かりやすさ・: Since names are identifiers, prioritize clarity and memorability while considering the balance among your characters. When naming fictional characters, giving them strange names can sometimes be effective for creating contrast.
texts.でも、自分の子供には『DQNネーム』を付けないように気を付けよう。将来、名前が原: However, be careful not to give your own children "DQN names." If your child becomes a delinquent in the future because of their name, it would be an unbearable situation.
